principles: An audit claim must be backed by a durable artifact, not by a validation that discards its input.
Prefer append-only history over mutable last-write-wins fields, so repeated reopens each leave their own record.
Additive-only changes to shared event shapes: existing consumers and shape tests must stay byte-identical.
Keep a LOW-severity cleanup minimal (YAGNI); do not smuggle unrelated hardening into the same change.
Never manufacture process evidence to satisfy a gate.
drivers: A codex host-B review found the reason validated but dropped, making the 'gated and auditable' claim false in its second half.
phase_transition events are already append-only and already emitted only after a successful phase write.
The user explicitly directed that the two comment corrections be separate low-priority items, not folded into the audit fix.
The repo has many parallel stories, so a shared-event change must not perturb other consumers.

options.name: additive-phase-transition-fields
pros: Reuses the existing append-only phase_transition event, so each reopen keeps its own historical record.
No new event type, storage, or reader; the event already carries storyId/fromPhase/toPhase/timestamp.
Strictly additive optional fields set only on REOPEN, so normal transitions stay byte-identical.
Emitted only after a successful writeStory, so no event can claim a transition that did not happen.
cons: Adds two keys to a widely-consumed event shape, requiring a backward-compat audit of consumers.
Does not by itself add actor/eventId provenance.

options.name: dedicated-reopen-audit-event
pros: A dedicated reopen_audit event type would isolate reopen provenance from the generic transition event.
Room for a richer bespoke schema.
cons: Requires a new ProcessEventType plus new readers, for a LOW-severity cleanup (violates YAGNI).
Introduces a second write that can diverge from the phase_transition event, creating exactly the transition/audit inconsistency the review warns about.

options.name: mutable-story-index-field
pros: A reopenReason field on the story index would be trivial to write and read.
cons: Mutable and last-write-wins: a second reopen silently overwrites the first, destroying history.
Splits audit data across mutable fields, which the reviewer explicitly called insufficient for a real audit chain.

rationale: Option additive-phase-transition-fields makes the audit claim true with the smallest possible change and the strongest history guarantee. The phase_transition event is already append-only and already emitted only after a successful writeStory, so carrying the reason there yields a per-reopen record and inherits the correct failure semantics for free, with no new event type or reader. Option mutable-story-index-field was rejected because a single mutable field loses history on a second reopen. Option dedicated-reopen-audit-event was rejected as disproportionate for a LOW finding and because a second independent write could diverge from the phase write. The additive-only shape (fields present only on REOPEN) was chosen specifically so the existing builder shape test and every existing consumer remain byte-identical.

preMortem.scenario: A phase_transition consumer somewhere validates the event's exact key set, or hashes/signs the serialized event, so the two new keys break it or change a signature.
preMortem.trigger: A consumer performs strict schema validation or includes the whole event in a hash domain.
preMortem.consequence: Gate failures or signature mismatches on unrelated stories that merely read transition events.
preMortem.mitigation: Enumerate every phase_transition consumer and confirm none does key-set validation, hashing, or full-event equality; confirm ProcessEvent uses an open index signature; keep the fields absent (not undefined) on normal transitions; run flow-stability (builder deepEqual) and process-fact-contract before REVIEW.

preMortem.scenario: The new fields leak onto NON-reopen transitions, changing the event shape for every story in the repo.
preMortem.trigger: The conditional is written on args.reason instead of on eventType, so any caller passing a stray reason pollutes normal transitions.
preMortem.consequence: Every phase_transition event repo-wide changes shape, breaking the shape test and potentially other parallel stories.
preMortem.mitigation: Gate the spread strictly on eventType === 'REOPEN' (the value only assigned for the PLAN->INIT remap), and assert in the smoke that a normal transition's event is unchanged; the builder deepEqual test covers the no-fields path.

preMortem.scenario: The reason is persisted but the test that proves it is a tautology, so a future refactor silently drops persistence again.
preMortem.trigger: Asserting against a mock/in-memory object rather than the real persisted JSONL, or writing the test after the code so it never failed.
preMortem.consequence: The audit guarantee regresses undetected and the same finding returns.
preMortem.mitigation: Write the assertion first and confirm it RED before implementing; read the event back through StoryStore.readProcessEvents (real JSONL) in the existing round-trip smoke rather than asserting on a constructed object.

preMortem.scenario: The two comment corrections get folded into the behavioral commit, so a reviewer nit on wording blocks the audit fix.
preMortem.trigger: Committing all three tasks together for convenience.
preMortem.consequence: Acceptance criteria blur and a LOW documentation quibble can stall the real fix, contradicting the explicit user directive.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep three separate single-purpose commits (one behavioral, two comment-only) and record the separation in the scope boundary.
